paragraphs: Yehudah ben Gerim: both parents were converts—Rashi, Shabbat 33b. The Jerusalem Talmud calls him bar Giyori. R. Shimon ben Yochai's student. R. Shimon ben Yochai sent his son to receive a blessing from Yehudah and R. Yonatan ben Akhmai. Heilprin calls the reading R. Shimon ben Chalafta in Tosafot a scribal error. [Moed Katan 9a reads Yonatan ben Asmai.] Because he related R. Shimon ben Yochai's criticism of this nation, the government heard and wished to kill R. Shimon, who hid in a cave thirteen years. After leaving the cave, R. Shimon saw Yehudah and set his eyes upon him. Yehudah died: Shabbat, Bameh Madlikin. Tosafot writes not to read “he became a heap of bones,” since he was a great scholar, as Moed Katan, chapter 1, implies. R. Yitzchak and R. Yochanan went to hear Torah from R. Shimon ben Yochai: Bereshit Rabbah, section 35. [The checked Midrash also names R. Yudan Giyori.] Novlot Chokhmah, 194b, writes that R. Shimon ben Yochai was Moses's soul and fled the government as Moses fled Pharaoh. Yehudah ben Gerim, who told the king, was the Egyptian's reincarnation; he made him a heap of bones as Moses did the Egyptian. But the Gemara and Rashi imply he did not tell the king directly: it became known to the king. Tosafot does not read “he became a heap of bones.”
